subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting gain a process-independent lifecycle or alert owner for Gateway memory-pressure and restart cases, or is startup accounting plus operator diagnostics sufficient?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a single mechanical bug fix: maintainers need to choose whether OpenClaw should own alert delivery outside the Gateway process and what macOS repro threshold proves the memory issue fixed.

options.title: Add independent failure alerting
options.body: Introduce or designate a durable owner that records cron started/success/error state and can alert after Gateway stalls or restarts, then prove it on macOS launchd.

options.title: Limit to Gateway restart accounting
options.body: Accept the current startup failed-run recovery and diagnostics as sufficient, while treating missed live alerts during a wedged Gateway as operator-visible rather than product-owned.

options.title: Close after disproving current leak
options.body: Run a fresh current-main macOS launchd memory-pressure proof and close only if it shows the original long-running Gateway heap/RSS growth and alert loss no longer reproduce.

recommendation.title: Add independent failure alerting
recommendation.body: Introduce or designate a durable owner that records cron started/success/error state and can alert after Gateway stalls or restarts, then prove it on macOS launchd.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears in recent history for both memory-core/provider work and cron runtime behavior, making him the best available cross-surface owner for the product boundary choice.
